segments.english: §10. And now, with the help of the Name, may He be blessed, let us return to the main point of our question, which we asked you to inform us according to the system of the Kabbalists, whom do we call upon in our prayers, and bless all our blessings and our worship, and from whom do we seek forgiveness and atonement. And your answer was in the words of a grumbler, like ravers: he claimed wheat from him, and he admitted barley to him, and you deny what is known and famous in their books to all, like one who swears about the man that he is a woman, and about the woman that she is a man, and about a pillar of marble that it is gold. And your anger burned against the book Metzaref ha-Emunah, and you mocked it and scorned it, and you called it the book the Mesharef etc., and thereby you revealed to all that you are the one who scorns the sages; and as to our questions: since Ze'ir Anpin, according to their words, is our God, and he feeds us and sustains us, and Him we worship; if so, all the worlds above the World of Emanation, who feeds and sustains them? If he casts their flow and their sustenance from below upward, and they worship and bow down to him, or perhaps their God fed and sustained them, he being the First Cause, and Him they worship, and we worship Ze'ir Anpin, who feeds us and sustains us? And if so, is the God of the upper ones not the God of the lower ones, God forbid? And this is the point of contradiction which we asked you to inform us and to instruct us, and to this your answer came: that the case is not like the proof, and does one bring proof to overturn a halakha given to Moses at Sinai? And that the sages of Kabbalah say thus: they received it from Moses.

כמתלהמים echoes דברי נרגן כמתלהמים (Prov 18:8, 26:22). The verses' sense (delicacies / wounds / something swallowed greedily) does not fit the author's use; he means those who rave. Proposed ruling: 'ravers' (cf. מתלהלה, Prov 26:18), with this note and the apparatus entry.
the case of one who claims wheat and the other admits barley (an answer that does not meet the claim); the English keeps the image
Metzaref ha-Emunah: 'the refining of faith', a book title, transliterated
the Mesharef: a pun on Metzaref ha-Emunah; 'mesharef' (a burner) for 'metzaref' (a refiner)
etc.: the author's own mark that the quotation is cut short
Ze'ir Anpin: 'Small Face', the name of a partzuf; the name is transliterated and its sense given here at its first occurrence in the unit
'our God' is the author's report of the Kabbalists' view ('according to their words')
ואותו: the wording of Deut 6:13 ('and Him you shall worship'), see apparatus
he: the question opens with the pronoun, 'he casts'
the flow (השפע) with the suffix 'their'
אלהיהם with singular verbs and 'he being the First Cause': 'their God'; the form is plural, and 'their gods' is the alternative
cause: the First Cause (עלה הראשונה)
plural construct 'elohei' with the singular verb 'eino'; 'God' by the ruling; the alternative is 'gods'
ח"ו: God forbid
ש continues 'your answer came: that ...'; the clause has no main verb of its own, so the English keeps 'that'
Kabbalah: the word for the tradition the Kabbalists claim; here it is 'the sages of Kabbalah'

grammar: והיתה (3:10.28) is a vav-prefixed perfect in the consecutive sense, 'and your answer was'; the subject 'your answer' follows the verb.
The verbs of 3:10.59-72 (וחרה, והלעגת, ובזית, וקראת) are a series of waw-prefixed perfects, each a separate verb of the sentence, so the English keeps them as a series.
ואם כן (3:10.136) opens a question. אלהי העליונים is a plural construct with the singular verb אינו; the English reads 'the God of' (see the token note on 3:10.138).
ועל שאלותינו (3:10.82) has no verb of its own: it is a topic phrase, and the main clause is the question that begins אם כן (3:10.97).

אם זורק הוא שפעם ופרנסתם מלמטה למעלה (3:10.108-114): 'from below upward' goes with the verb זורק, and 'their flow' and 'their sustenance' are both its objects; the lower beings are the ones that send the flow up. The upper worlds are those that 'worship and bow down' (עובדים ומשתחוים, 3:10.116-117).

The simile כמתלהמים טענו חטים והודה לו בשעורים (3:10.32-37): טענו is 'he claimed from him' (the verb with an object suffix) and והודה 'and he admitted': one claims wheat and the other admits barley, the Mishnaic case of a claim answered by an admission of something else, so that the answer misses the claim. כמתלהמים follows דברי נרגן as in Prov 18:8 and 26:22 (see apparatus).
apparatus: Base text: the Wikisource transcription of the paragraph; not yet collated against the 1931 scan (Q2 default: flagged until collated).

Echo of Prov 18:8 and 26:22 ('דברי נרגן כמתלהמים'): 'in the words of a grumbler, like ravers' (3:10.30-32). The sense of מתלהמים in the verses is itself disputed; here the context decides (cf. Prov 26:18, 'like a madman').
Echo of Deut 6:13 ('The LORD your God you shall fear, and Him you shall worship'): 'and Him we worship' (3:10.95-96).

segments.english: §11. We are very astonished and amazed at your words and at this reply of yours, and is it a halakha given to Moses at Sinai to believe in many divinities? And to worship other gods apart from the LORD our God, the First, and Rock of all? And He is the cause of all causes, all of them, and with deceit you came in these replies of yours to stubborn-hearted people, whom you boasted over, and showed them these words of yours, saying: "See, I have overturned their words, and rejected their proofs in haste," and your pamphlet goes round to all the diners, and after they praised and lauded you, that you are sharp and keen, you brought it to us. And behold, all of it is deceptions, as if you did not know what our question turns on, and to this false error of yours we shall return again, since it is known and famous in the rules of the decisors (Kenesset ha-Gedolah, the Radbaz, and Sh"Z), that wherever the Kabbalah disagrees with the ruling, one goes after the ruling, and this rule is famous in Israel. And if your words are that this Kabbalah is a halakha given to Moses at Sinai, and do you reject a halakha given to Moses on account of the reasoning of some tanna or amora, and all the more so a later decisor (see below, §15), and you must bring a proof and inform us where we have found this, that any tanna or amora would be so bold to dispute and to rule against the halakha received from Moses our teacher, peace be upon him. Would he not be called a fool, or a wicked and arrogant man? And in many places in the Talmud it is a saying in the mouths of the Rabbis to say: "If it is a halakha, we accept it, and if it is reasoning, there is an answer."

tokens.note: printed section number (יא), the author's own section label
rhetorical question, as the Hebrew has it (וכי)
divinities: the plural is counted ('many'), so the English is plural
other gods: the wording of Exod 20:3 (see apparatus)
the LORD: the Tetragrammaton, written ה' in the text
the First: an allusion to Isa 44:6 (see apparatus)
את here is the second-person pronoun 'you', the subject, not the object marker
אלה modifies בתשובותיך ('these replies of yours'), not the people
לאמר introduces the quotation, which ends at בקש (3:11.56); what follows is the author's voice

בקש is read as ב + קש, 'with straw': to dismiss with a straw is to dismiss lightly, without effort (the Talmudic idiom of pushing aside with a straw or reed). Proposed ruling: 'rejected their proofs with a straw' (note: 'dismissed lightly'). 'In haste' and 'in brief' are not supported by the word.
קונדריס: a small book, a pamphlet
המסובין: those reclining at a meal
כנה"ג: Kenesset ha-Gedolah ('the Great Assembly'), a book, written out
ורדב"ז: the Radbaz (David ibn Zimra)
ושה"ז: the abbreviation is not expanded here, since its expansion is not established; kept as written
סי': the author's section number, §15
יעיז פניו: 'brazen his face', the idiom for daring
רבי': רבינו, 'our teacher', of Moses; the fixed form 'Moses our teacher'
ע"ה: peace be upon him
מרגלא בפומיהו דרבנן: a common saying in the Aramaic of the Talmud, as the author gives it
the saying is quoted without a reference in the author's text; nothing is added

דין in the saying 'אם הלכה נקבל ואם לדין יש תשובה' means reasoning (a logical argument), as against a received halakha; it is not a court's verdict. Proposed ruling: render דין as 'reasoning' in this saying, with this note; 'judgment' is not used.

grammar: הלכה למשה מסיני להאמין (3:11.11-16) and ולעבוד (3:11.18) are infinitives after the question 'is it a halakha': 'to believe' and 'to worship' are its content.
את in ובמרמה את בא (3:11.32-34) is the second-person pronoun 'you', the subject, not the object marker; the English reads 'you came'.

ראו כי סתרתי ... בקש (3:11.48-56) is the quotation that follows לאמר (3:11.47). It ends at בקש: וחוזר קונדריסך ('your pamphlet goes round') and הבאת אותה לנו ('you brought it to us') speak of the respondent in the second person and of the questioners as 'us', so they are the author's voice, not the respondent's.
אלה in בתשובותיך אלה (3:11.35-36) belongs to 'your replies' ('these replies of yours'), not to the people that follow.
מרגלא בפומיהו דרבנן (3:11.165-168) is Bavli Aramaic, the frame of the saying; the saying itself (3:11.169-175) is in Hebrew, quoted without a reference.
ואם לדין יש תשובה (3:11.172-175): דין here is reasoning (a logical argument), set against a received halakha; 'judgment' would read as a court's verdict.
apparatus: Allusion to Isa 44:6 ('I am the first and I am the last, and besides Me there is no God'): 'the First' (3:11.24).
Allusion to Isa 44:8 ('Is there a God besides Me? There is no Rock; I know none'): 'and Rock' (3:11.25), and 'other' with מבלעדי (3:11.21).
Allusion to Exod 20:3 ('You shall have no other gods before Me'): 'other gods' (3:11.19-20).
ושה"ז (3:11.95): an unclear abbreviation; kept as written in the English and not expanded. No conjecture is offered.
